What I'm watching this week, and why.

Bitcoin is ranging. No clean trend either way, score 50/100, open interest -4.9% in 24h.

Ranges are where accounts die quietly: every breakout looks real, every fade looks smart, and you pay for both. The only thing that has worked for me in a range is waiting for the edge of it and sizing small. Boring on purpose.

I spent ten years in business analysis before crypto. The habit that carried over: decide what would prove you wrong before you decide what you want to be true.

What's the one level or data point you're watching this week?

Mid-week read on Bitcoin, in plain language.

Everyone wants a direction call. Here's what the data actually says:

→ $BTC Fusion Score: 50/100 — not enough conviction either way
→ Smart Money verdict: neutral
→ Market regime: Ranging

Nobody has an edge here, including the people who sound certain. A score in the middle means the layers disagree with each other, and when they disagree the market usually chops until one side gives up. My rule in this state: no new positions, smaller size if I'm already in, and I write down what would change my mind before it does.

I put these layers on one screen because I used to make the opposite mistake: trading the chart and finding out about the positioning afterwards.

What's your read on the current structure?

Risk management isn't exciting. But it's the only reason we're still profitable.

I coded these rules directly into the algorithm — they can't be overridden:

→ Max 3 new trades per day — prevents overtrading in FOMO conditions

→ 2h cooldown between same ticker — stops revenge trading

→ Mandatory stop-loss at entry — no trade exists without an invalidation

→ 5-day max hold — zombie positions get cut automatically

→ Smart Money veto — even a perfect score gets rejected if institutional flow disagrees

→ Minimum 1.0 R:R — no trade with more risk than reward

→ tradingventureclub.com/results.html
